function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake, plus a few tips on choosing the right spot for your needs:

| Option | What it offers | When it’s best |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for special occasions | If you want a personal touch, support a small business, or need something unique (e.g., gluten‑free, vegan). |
| **Online cake delivery services** (e.g., Goldbelly, Cake Delivery, or regional sites) | Nationwide delivery, curated selections from top bakers | For a wide variety of flavors, premium ingredients, or when you’re ordering from afar. |
| **Grocery stores & supermarkets** (e.g., Kroger, Safeway, Walmart) | Ready‑made cakes, seasonal specials, sometimes custom orders | Convenient for last‑minute needs or if you’re already shopping nearby. |
| **Specialty dessert shops** (e.g., Magnolia Bakery, Levain Bakery) | Signature cakes, artisanal pastries | If you’re looking for a particular brand or style. |
| **Restaurant chains** (e.g., Starbucks, Panera Bread) | Simple store‑bought cakes, often pre‑packaged | Quick pick‑up, no waiting time. |
| **DIY kits** (e.g., King Arthur Baking, Bakeology) | All‑in‑one kits to bake at home | Fun for a baking project or if you want to customize the design yourself. |

### How to choose:
1. **Occasion & Size** – Local bakeries excel at custom sizes and designs; grocery stores are great for standard sizes.
2. **Dietary Needs** – Look for bakeries that specialize in gluten‑free, vegan, or allergy‑friendly options.
3. **Delivery Time** – Online services usually have a delivery window; local shops can offer same‑day pickup or delivery.
4. **Budget** – DIY kits and grocery store cakes tend to be cheaper; specialty bakeries and online deliveries can be pricier.

---

#### Quick next steps:
1. **Tell me your city or zip code** so I can give you a list of nearby bakeries or delivery services.
2. **Let me know the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate event) and any dietary restrictions.
3. **Decide on a budget range** (e.g., $20–$50, $50–$100).

Once I have those details, I’ll pull up a shortlist of places you can order from, complete with links, reviews, and contact info. Let me know!
